extracted.intended_audience: auditors, institutional financial aid administrators, and compliance officers performing A-133 audits of Student Financial Assistance (Title IV and related HHS) programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for auditing and administering the Student Financial Assistance Cluster (Title IV and related HHS programs), describing program eligibility, allowable uses, cash management, matching, earmarking, loan limits, scholarship rules, reporting, and related compliance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities Allowed or Unallowed (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, SFA funds can be used only for making awards to students and for administration of the programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other allowable uses vary by specific program; auditors should consult program-specific rules for exceptions and detailed limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Perkins Loan (FPL) allowable uses and transfer rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain billing, collection, and litigation costs must first be charged to the borrower and cannot be charged to the loan fund; limited use of program funds for collection costs when borrower payments are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schools may transfer up to 25% of their Federal Capital Contribution for an award year to FSEOG or FWS, and may transfer up to 100% of initial and supplemental allocations to an approved Work Colleges program. Transferred funds must be used per the receiving program's requirements and unexpended funds must be returned to Perkins at year end (34 CFR sections 674.8, 674.18, 674.47, 675.41).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Work Study (FWS) allowable uses
rubrics_metrics.description: FWS funds may be used only for awards to students, Job Location and Development (JLD) Program, Work-Colleges Program, administrative costs, and transfers to FSEOG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must provide matching funds unless they request and receive 100% Federal share in their FISAP (34 CFR sections 675.18 and 675.33).

rubrics_metrics.name: HPSL/PCL and NSL allowable uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may be used for capital distribution, certain litigation costs (as agreed by Secretary), credit bureau membership costs, approved collection costs, and repayment of principal/interest on Federal capital loans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use and limits specified at HPSL (42 CFR section 57.205(a)) and NSL (42 CFR section 57.305(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Loan origination and booking requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct Loan is an electronic program with four types of cycles (Loan Origination Records, Promissory Note Manifests, Disbursement Records, Change Records). A loan is 'booked' when the institution transmits and the LOC accepts: (1) loan origination record, (2) promissory note manifest matched with paper note, and (3) first disbursement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The borrower's original accepted promissory note is maintained at the LOC; the institution need not keep a copy. Institutions participate in various origination options and must follow Direct Loan School Guide procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash Management (payment methods and disbursement timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: ED pays institutions in advance, by reimbursement, or by cash monitoring methods; pilot just-in-time (JIT) is used in some cases. Under reimbursement and cash monitoring, institutions must disburse funds to students before requesting funds from ED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under advance payments, requests must not exceed amount immediately needed and disbursements must be made as soon as administratively feasible and no later than three business days after receipt. Excess cash not disbursed by the end of the third business day is generally excess cash and must be returned, with tolerance rules: during peak period <3% of prior-year drawdowns, otherwise <1%, and eliminated within seven calendar days. Interest earnings > $250 must be returned to ED except Perkins earnings are reinvested in the revolving fund (34 CFR sections 668.162 and 166). HHS programs require new FCC requests only when needed and idle cash/interest deposited in income-producing accounts with excess returned to HHS (HPSL and NSL regs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for Individuals – financial need determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Student eligibility requirements are in Appendix A; determination of SFA award amounts is based on financial need, generally COA minus financial resources reasonably available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Title IV, financial resources available generally equal the Expected Family Contribution (EFC) computed by the central processor (on SAR/ISIR). For HHS programs and FPL, schools must use national need analysis systems or Secretary-approved procedures and may consider other school information. Schools must document criteria used for special costs and may use professional judgment to adjust COA for special circumstances (citations across program regs provided). COA components include tuition/fees, allowance for books/supplies/transportation/miscellaneous, room/board, dependent care where applicable, study abroad/co-op costs, disability-related costs, and loan fees; with exceptions for <half-time, correspondence, incarcerated students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination of awards among programs and other aid
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards must be coordinated among various programs and with other Federal and non-Federal aid to ensure total aid is not awarded in excess of the student's financial need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific cross-program coordination citations: FPL, FWS, FSEOG (34 CFR sections 673.5 and 673.6); FFEL (34 CFR section 682.603); Direct Loan (34 CFR section 685.301); HPSL and NSL regs; auditors should verify coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: HPSL / PCL and NSL loan limits and selection rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For periods prior to Nov 13, 1998 HPSL annual total to a student may not exceed $2,500 plus tuition; for later periods amounts may not exceed COA (with special allowances for 3rd/4th year med students to cover loan balances). NSL annual limits: generally $2,500, up to $4,000 for final two academic years; aggregate NSL cap $13,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For HPSL/medical students selection must be based on greatest financial need considering other resources (42 CFR sections cited). After Nov 13, 1998 statutory/topline changes apply (PHSA amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship Program for Students of Exceptional Financial Need (EFN) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarships awarded to eligible health profession students must include tuition, fees and reasonable educational expenses and recipients must agree to practice primary care; if recipient ceases full-time status, school discontinues scholarship and returns unused balance to Federal Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program authority was repealed by Health Professions Education Partnership Act of 1998; transitional provisions maintain existing agreements per statute (42 USC and 42 CFR citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarships for Disadvantaged Students – eligibility and allowable expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards to full-time students from disadvantaged backgrounds with financial need enrolled or accepted in a health profession program; scholarships may be expended only for tuition, other reasonable educational expenses, and reasonable living expenses incurred in attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program authority and statutory citations: 42 USC 294; section 737 of PHSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pell Grant award determination procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Six-step process to determine Pell awards: (1) determine enrollment status, (2) calculate COA (based on full-time/full academic year; prorate if program length differs), (3) determine annual award from Payment/Disbursement Schedule using COA and EFC, (4) determine payment period (terms = term), (5) calculate payment for payment periods (varies by formula/length/alternative calculations), (6) disburse funds at prescribed times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment/Disbursement Schedules provided annually by ED; special rules for prorating costs when enrolled less than half-time, allowable cost components for <half-time; see Pell Grant Reference in Federal SFA Handbook and regs 34 CFR sections 690.61–690.67 and 690.75–690.78.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campus-Based programs award limits and COA calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum award under campus-based programs equals student's financial need (COA minus EFC) minus aid from other SFA and other resources. For programs of study or enrollment periods less or greater than an academic year, COA for loans and campus-based aid is based on student's actual costs for the period rather than prorated full-year costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial aid administrators have discretion in awarding amounts among programs, subject to statutory/regulatory limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: FSEOG priority, award amounts, and matching
rubrics_metrics.description: FSEOG grants given to eligible undergraduate students with priority to Pell recipients having lowest EFC; institution decides amount up to $4,000 and not less than $100 per academic year (may increase to $4,400 for approved study abroad). Federal funds are matched with institutional funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 34 CFR sections 676.10, 676.20 and matching rules in 34 CFR section 676.21 for Federal share limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual loan maximums for subsidized loans (FPL/Direct/FFEL tiers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Undergraduate subsidized annual limits vary by year-of-study: first-year not completed $2,625; second-year not completed up to $3,500; third-year+ up to $5,500; graduate/professional up to $8,500 per academic year. Programs shorter than an academic year require proration; programs < one-third academic year ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations to 34 CFR section 674.7 (moving to 674.12) and Federal SFA Handbook; table-like guidance provided for auditors to test compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual limits for unsubsidized loans
rubrics_metrics.description: Unsubsidized loan amounts equal difference between eligible subsidized amount and amount received, or difference between COA and estimated financial assistance. Additional unsubsidized eligibility for independent students and dependent students with exceptional circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts: students who have not completed first two undergraduate years up to $4,000; students who completed first two years up to $5,000; graduate/professional students up to $10,000 per academic year. Proration rules apply for programs shorter than an academic year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions – increased loan limits for former HEAL borrowers
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain health professions students who previously borrowed under HEAL are authorized increased annual loan limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Dear Colleague Letters GEN-96-14, GEN-97-4, GEN-97-14, GEN-98-18, GEN-98-23, GEN-99-21 and subsequent letters for details (available on IFAP website).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate loan limits (subsidized + unsubsidized)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate loan limits are $23,000 for dependent undergraduates, $46,000 for independent undergraduates, and $138,500 (including $65,500 subsidized and $73,000 unsubsidized) for graduate/professional students (includes undergraduate borrowings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits are cumulative across FFEL and Direct Loan programs; auditors should verify combined borrowing does not exceed these caps (34 CFR sections 682.204 and 685.203).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent PLUS loan limits
rubrics_metrics.description: PLUS loans limited to parent borrowers and may not exceed the student's estimated COA minus other financial aid awarded during the period of enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant regs: FFEL (34 CFR sections 682.201 and 682.204); Direct Loan (34 CFR sections 685.200 and 685.203).

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching requirements – Federal Perkins Loan (ICC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution's matching share (Institutional Capital Contribution, ICC) is one third of the Federal Capital Contribution (FCC) (or 25% of combined FCC and ICC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory/regulatory citation: 34 CFR section 674.8; auditors should verify ICC deposits and maintenance of revolving fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching requirements – FSEOG Federal share limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal share of FSEOG awards may not exceed 75% of total FSEOG awards made by the school, though the Secretary may authorize 100% Federal funding if conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference: 34 CFR section 676.21; auditors should verify matched institutional funds and any Secretary-authorized exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching requirements – FWS Federal share and special allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal share of FWS compensation for students employed other than by private-for-profit organizations generally may not exceed 75% of total FWS awards; allowed up to 90% for up to 10% of students under specific nonprofit/government employment conditions; Federal share for private-for-profit employers limited to 50%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two situations permit 100% Federal share: (1) institution designated under Title III Strengthening Institutions or HBCU program and requested increased share as part of FWS application; (2) student employed as reading tutor or family literacy tutor where work performed for institution, public agency, or private nonprofit (34 CFR section 675.26; 42 USC citation). Auditors should verify employer type, approvals, and percentage limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching requirements – HPSL/NSL ICC
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution's matching share (ICC) for HPSL/NSL is one ninth of the FCC and must be deposited in a health professions student loan fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory citations: 42 CFR sections 57.202 and 57.302; auditors should verify deposit and accounting of ICC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earmarking – FWS community service requirement and JLD limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions shall use at least 5% of their FWS allocation for compensating students employed in community service activities (increases to 7% beginning July 1, 2000) unless waived by the Secretary. An institution may use up to 10% of its FWS or $50,000 (whichever is less) for a JLD program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory citations: 34 CFR sections 675.18 and 675.32; auditors should verify earmarked amounts and waivers if any.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Income – Federal Perkins Loan revolving fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal and interest repayments made by students and reimbursements for canceled loans are reinvested in the Federal Perkins Loan revolving fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory citation: 34 CFR section 674.8; auditors should verify reinvestment and fund accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting – financial reporting forms applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain standard federal financial reporting forms are noted as not applicable to these programs in this context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SF-269 (Financial Status Report), SF-270 (Request for Advance or Reimbursement), SF-271 (Outlay Report and Request for Reimbursement for Construction), and SF-272 (Federal Cash Transactions Report) are listed as Not Applicable for this cluster context; auditors should follow program-specific reporting requirements elsewhere in the supplement and Federal SFA Handbook.
